source_text: Quod igitur libris tuis, senex Augustine, retinetur: Libido exorta est post peccatum, quam coacti sunt velare confusi [n203] .
pass_a_gloss: What therefore is retained in your books, old Augustine: Lust has arisen after sin, which the confused have been forced to veil.

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise often sexual desire; Julian treats as created sensation, not a sin-nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: What your books contain, then, old Augustine, is this: ‘Desire arose after sin, and their confusion forced them to cover it’ (Genesis 3:7) (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.36; compare Genesis 3:7).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.display: Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.36; compare Genesis 3:7
bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
